the single tube tetraplect qPCR assay for the detection of MTBC members in clinical samples of suspected EPTB cases was a sensitive and rapid method that could be used as a diagnostic tool for the detection of TB in addition to conventional microbiological methods.
a rapid and sensitive qPCR assay could be used as a first-line test for TB detection and identification of MTBC members in clinical samples.
we evaluated the performance of MTBC-RD q-PCR for EPTB diagnosis and MTBC members differentiation directly on extrapulpontaneous samples.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a rapid, simple and sensitive molecular method for the simultaneous detection of MTBC and identification of MTBC members from EPTB clinical samples.
a rapid and sensitive method for TB diagnosis and differentiation between MTB, M. bovis BCG and other MTBC members.
the development of a new molecular diagnostic test that could improve the diagnosis of TB in Tunisia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MTBC–RDqPCR assay could be used as an additional tool in the diagnosis of EPTB.
this qPCR assay is an accurate, rapid, and reliable method for simultaneous detection and identification of MTBC members in EPTB clinical samples.

this study is the first to describe the use of MTBC–RDqPCR for the detection and identification of MTBC members on extrapulmonay clinical samples from patients in Tunisia and the first to describe a single tube tetraphlex qPCR assay for the detection of MTBC and its members in extrapunomay samples in Africa.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the qPCR assay could be used as a first line screening tool for the rapid diagnosis of MTBC-mediated EPTB and the differentiation between the MTBC members.
MTBC-RD qRT-PCR could be a useful method for rapid detection of TB and MTBC members in extrapolmonary samples.
the qPCR assay is an important and useful tool for TB diagnosis, particularly in EPTB patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the qPCR assay is a useful tool in the diagnosis of EPTB.
qPCR could be used to identify MTBC members in EPTB cases in Tunisia.
the qPCR method can be used to rapidly and accurately identify M. tuberculosis complex members directly from EPTB clinical specimens.
